exposure: late-onset sepsis (LOS) status (no LOS, proven LOS, clinical LOS)
cohort: The study included 752 very low birth weight (VLBW) preterm infants, 23 to 33 gestational weeks and 400 to 1,500 g birth weight, admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit between 2008 and 2017 and who survived over 72 hours.
finding: Late-onset sepsis (LOS) had a high incidence and mortality in very low birth weight infants, with care interventions like mechanical ventilation and parenteral nutrition being key risk factors, and it was associated with increased risk of death, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and retinopathy of prematurity.
